title: Finite cone models for sheaf extensions and bounded truncation towers
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. Module sheaves, sheaf tensor products, derived categories and cohomology are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,A)$ for the completed integral category including compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and $Q:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=\mathcal C_X[1/\varpi]$ for its raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. A rational module sheaf is constructible when on a finite locally closed stratification it is pro-etale locally finite free [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Write $F_X(K)=E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$ and $J_X(QK)=F_X(K)$, $J_X(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)$ for the functor specified in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. Assume $J_X$ is fully faithful, and assume the integral degree-zero models for the finite filtration quotients provided in [lem-per-rational-stratum-integral-models]. Its isomorphism-closed essential image in $D(E_X)$ contains zero and all shifts and is closed under distinguished extensions. More precisely, for any triangle $J_X(QK_1)\to C\to J_X(QK_2)\xrightarrow{\delta}J_X(QK_1)[1]$, the unique lift of $\delta$ to $\mathcal R_X$ can be represented by an integral fraction $f/\varpi^n$, and a shifted integral cone of $f$ represents an object $QK$ with $J_X(QK)\cong C$. Rescaling by the invertible scalar $\varpi^n$ gives the cone comparison. Iterating this construction along any supplied finite filtration from [lem-per-rational-stratum-integral-models] gives a model for every constructible sheaf placed in degree zero. For any $C\in D(E_X)$ with bounded constructible cohomology and any interval $[a,b]$ containing its nonzero cohomology, the finite standard truncation tower [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] similarly gives $K\in\mathcal C_X$ and $J_X(QK)\cong C$. The construction uses only the integral models of the filtration pieces, finitely many lifted connecting arrows, shifts and cones. It uses no direct-summand or idempotent completion. The zero-cohomology case is the zero object. This is a conditional finite-cone construction, not a claim of full faithfulness or of functor/pullback coherence.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), reduction of essential surjectivity to local systems; expanded finite-filtration and truncation cone construction, pp. 61-62

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated], the actual category $\mathcal C_X$ with its compatible etale-origin witnesses contains zero and is closed under all integer shifts and cones. By [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor], $F_X$ is triangulated and $J_X(QK)=F_X(K)$. Consequently $J_X(Q0)\cong0$ and $J_X(Q(K[r]))\cong J_X(QK)[r]$ for every integer $r$. Composing these isomorphisms with any given image witness proves the zero and shift assertions for the isomorphism-closed essential image.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), triangulated source and scalar-localization functor; compatible-tower closure supplied by the cited node

proof.text: Write $U=J_X(QK_1)$ and $V=J_X(QK_2)$. Use the shift comparison to regard the connecting arrow $\delta:V\to U[1]$ as an arrow $J_X(QK_2)\to J_X(Q(K_1[1]))$. Full faithfulness, which is a hypothesis here, gives a unique arrow $\alpha:QK_2\to Q(K_1[1])$ mapping to it. By the definition of the raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], $\alpha$ is an element of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_X}(K_2,K_1[1])\otimes_A E$, and $Q$ sends an integral arrow $g$ to $g\otimes1$. Since $E=A[1/\varpi]$, every element $\sum_i g_i\otimes\varpi^{-n_i}$ of this tensor product equals $f\otimes\varpi^{-n}$ with $n=\max_i n_i\geq0$ and $f=\sum_i\varpi^{n-n_i}g_i:K_2\to K_1[1]$; hence $\varpi^n\alpha=f\otimes1=Q(f)$, i.e. $\alpha=f/\varpi^n$. The $E$-linearity of $J_X$ and the formula $J_X(Qf)=F_X(f)$ of [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor] give $F_X(f)=\varpi^n\delta$ after the same shift identification. Only $\alpha$ is unique; its numerator and denominator need not be.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), full faithfulness used to lift extension classes; explicit scalar-fraction argument

proof.text: Choose a cone triangle $K_2\xrightarrow{f}K_1[1]\to D\to K_2[1]$ using TR1 of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The closure theorem [lem-weil-pbc-uniform-complete-triangulated] gives $D\in\mathcal C_X$ and $K=D[-1]\in\mathcal C_X$, with the required witnesses. Applying the triangulated functor $F_X$ of [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor] gives a distinguished triangle $V\xrightarrow{F_X(f)}U[1]\to F_X(D)\to V[1]$.

source.place: Tag 0145, derived-definition-triangulated-category, TR1; integral closure and exact realization from the cited nodes

proof.text: Rotate the given triangle $U\xrightarrow{i}C\xrightarrow{p}V\xrightarrow{\delta}U[1]$ twice by TR2 of [def-weil-triangulated-category], obtaining $V\xrightarrow{\delta}U[1]\xrightarrow{-i[1]}C[1]\xrightarrow{-p[1]}V[1]$. Compare this with the image cone triangle of Step 3. On the first two vertices take $a=1_V$ and $b=\varpi^n1_{U[1]}$. The first square commutes because $b\delta=\varpi^n\delta=F_X(f)a$. Both maps are invertible, with inverses $1_V$ and $\varpi^{-n}1_{U[1]}$. TR3 completes them to a morphism of distinguished triangles, and [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes its third component $c:C[1]\to F_X(D)$ invertible. Shifting $c$ by $[-1]$ and using the shift comparison for $F_X$ gives $C\cong F_X(D[-1])=J_X(QK)$. This also proves extension closure when the endpoints are merely isomorphic to image objects, by conjugating their arrows by the given endpoint isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0145, TR2 and TR3; Tag 014A, lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle; explicit rescaling square

proof.text: Let $0=F_0\subset\cdots\subset F_m=F$ be any supplied finite filtration and let $M_k[0]\in\mathcal C_X$ be its supplied integral quotient models, as in [lem-per-rational-stratum-integral-models]. Exact scalar localization in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor] identifies $J_X(Q(M_k[0]))$ with $(F_k/F_{k-1})[0]$. Induct on $k$ with the assertion that an integral object $K_k$ and an isomorphism $J_X(QK_k)\cong F_k[0]$ have been constructed: take $K_0=0$. The short exact sequence $0\to F_{k-1}\to F_k\to F_k/F_{k-1}\to0$ gives a distinguished triangle in $D(E_X)$ by [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]. Conjugate its endpoints by the inductive isomorphism and the supplied quotient comparison; Steps 2-4 construct $K_k$ by one integral cone and shift. At $k=m$ this gives a model of $F[0]$. For $m=0$ the base case already gives it.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), finite filtration reduction; short-exact-sequence triangle is Stacks Tag 0152

proof.text: Now let $C$ have constructible cohomology vanishing outside $[a,b]$. By [def-kun-truncations], $\tau_{\leq a-1}C$ is acyclic and $\tau_{\leq b}C\to C$ induces isomorphisms on all cohomology. Choose a complex representing $C$. The map $0\to\tau_{\leq a-1}C$ of complexes is a quasi-isomorphism, and the truncation inclusion at $b$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Both become invertible in the derived category by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hence start the tower with the zero integral model of $\tau_{\leq a-1}C$ and end with the indicated isomorphism to $C$. If all cohomology vanishes, the same quasi-isomorphism $0\to C$ directly gives the zero model, without any tower.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, endpoints; Tag 05RU, derived localization at quasi-isomorphisms

proof.text: For each $r=a,\ldots,b$, the constructible sheaf $\mathcal H^r(C)$ has an integral degree-zero model by Step 5. Shift that model by $[-r]$. The successive-truncation triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] is $\tau_{\leq r-1}C\to\tau_{\leq r}C\to\mathcal H^r(C)[-r]\to(\tau_{\leq r-1}C)[1]$. Induct on $r$, starting with the zero model from Step 6: if a model of $\tau_{\leq r-1}C$ has been constructed, its isomorphism and the shifted sheaf model identify the endpoints of this triangle with image objects, so Steps 2-4 give an integral model of $\tau_{\leq r}C$. There are $b-a+1$ steps. The last model realizes $C$ by Step 6. All intermediate integral objects are shifts or cones of previously constructed objects; the sheaf models themselves use finite filtrations. Thus the entire construction is finite and uses no summand extraction or idempotent completion.
